1. Start with cylindrical stock sized to the printed 45.3 diameter and 80 length.
2. Turn the main body to the printed 38.4 diameter for the printed 58.7 length.
3. Turn the shoulder to the printed 45.3 diameter for the printed 21.3 length.
4. Drill the through hole to the printed 20 diameter along the full 80 length.
5. Chamfer the outer edge of the shoulder end face with a 2 chamfer.
6. Fillet the outer edge of the main body end face with a 2 radius.

1. Saw a blank from round bar stock with enough allowance to clean up at the printed ø45.3 maximum diameter and the 80 overall length (58.7 + 21.3).
2. Face both ends square and bring the blank to the finished overall length of 80, the sum of the printed 58.7 and 21.3.
3. Turn the main body to the printed ø38.4 over the printed 58.7 length measured from the base end.
4. Leave the remaining printed 21.3 at the far end as the boss and turn it to the printed ø45.3, forming the shoulder where the body ends.
5. Drill and bore the central through hole along the axis to the printed ø21.3, running the full length of the part.
6. Cut a shallow internal groove in the bore wall at the shoulder, sized to suit the mating seal.
7. Chamfer the outer rim of the boss end face with a small, even chamfer.
8. Fillet the outer rim of the base end face with a small radius to break the sharp edge.

1. Start with a solid cylindrical blank of 45.3 diameter and 80 length.
2. Turn the main body down to a 38.4 diameter for a length of 58.7 from the base.
3. Leave the remaining 21.3 of length at the full 45.3 diameter to form the shoulder.
4. Drill a through hole of 20 diameter along the center axis.
5. Chamfer the outer edge of the shoulder end face with a 3 chamfer.
6. Fillet the outer edge of the base end face with a 2 radius.

1. Start with cylindrical stock of diameter 38.4 and length 80.
2. Turn the main body to the printed diameter of 38.4 for a length of 58.7.
3. Turn the shoulder section to the printed diameter of 45.3 for a length of 21.3.
4. Drill the through hole to the printed diameter of 20.
5. Cut the keyway slot to the printed width of 5 and depth of 4.
6. Chamfer the end edge to the printed size of 3.
7. Fillet the shoulder transition to the printed radius of 2.

1. Start with cylindrical stock sized to the printed 45.3 diameter and cut it to the printed 80 length.
2. Turn the main body down to the printed 38.4 diameter over the printed 58.7 length.
3. Leave the remaining printed 21.3 length at the full printed 45.3 diameter to form the flange.
4. Drill the central through hole along the axis to the printed 15.2 diameter.
5. Chamfer the outer edge of the flange end face.
6. Fillet the shoulder where the body meets the flange.

1. Start with cylindrical stock sized to the printed 45.3 maximum diameter and the printed 80 overall length, which is the sum of the printed 58.7 and 21.3.
2. Turn the main body to the printed ø38.4 diameter for the printed 58.7 length.
3. Turn the raised shoulder to the printed ø45.3 diameter for the printed 21.3 length at the end of the body.
4. Bore the through hole to the printed ø28 diameter along the full length of the part.
5. Cut the internal thread in the bore to the printed ø30 major diameter with the printed 2 pitch.
6. Chamfer the outer edge of the shoulder end face with the printed 3 chamfer size.

1. Saw a blank from round bar stock, leaving machining allowance on the diameter and on both end faces.
2. Turn the main body to the printed ø38.4 outside diameter, holding that diameter over the printed 58.7 length measured from the base end.
3. Turn the raised end boss to the printed ø45.3 diameter, leaving it standing 21.3 tall above the body shoulder.
4. Face the boss end so the overall length from the base face to the boss face is the sum of the printed 58.7 and 21.3.
5. Drill and bore the through hole along the axis so the body is left as an open sleeve with a uniform wall.
6. Chamfer the outer rim of the boss end face with a small, even chamfer.
7. Round the outer rim of the base end face with a small fillet to finish the part.

1. Saw a blank from round bar stock with enough diameter to clean up at the ø45.3 shoulder and enough length to face both ends.
2. Face the blank and turn the main body to ø38.4 for a length of 58.7.
3. Turn the shoulder to ø45.3 over the remaining 21.3 of length, leaving a clean step where the two diameters meet.
4. Face the free end of the shoulder so the overall length is 80, the sum of 58.7 and 21.3.
5. Drill and bore the ø38.4 hole in from the free end, stopping short of the step so the body stays hollow with a closed bottom.
6. Drill the small through hole on the centerline of the closed end, passing through the bottom of the bore.
7. Chamfer the outer rim of the shoulder's free end with a small, even chamfer.
8. Round the rim of the closed end with a small fillet to break the sharp edge.

1. Start with stock sufficient to form an 80 long by 42.9 wide by 34.8 high block.
2. Mill the base profile to the 80 length and 42.9 width, leaving the full 34.8 height.
3. Cut the top contour so the left end rises to the 42.9 width while the right end tapers to the 20 width.
4. Machine the step where the 42.9 width transitions down to the 20 width across the 80 length.
5. Drill the first hole at the location set by the 34.8 dimension from the left end.
6. Drill the second hole at the location set by the 34.8 dimension from the right end.
7. Apply the R2.7 fillet to the bottom right corner.
8. Apply the R5.4 fillet to the top left corner.
9. Apply the R6.7 fillet to the top right corner.
10. Apply the R16.1 fillet to the step corner where the width changes.

1. Start with stock sufficient to produce an 80 long by 42.9 wide by 34.8 high block.
2. Mill the base profile to the 80 length and 42.9 width, leaving the full 34.8 height.
3. Cut the top contour so the left end rises to the 42.9 width while the right end tapers to the 34.8 width.
4. Form the large rounded shoulder at the left end to the R16.1 radius.
5. Form the smaller rounded transition at the right end to the R6.7 radius.
6. Form the lower rounded corner at the left end to the R5.2 radius.
7. Form the lower rounded corner at the right end to the R2.7 radius.
8. Apply the 2× R5.4 rounds to the two remaining vertical edges.

1. Start with stock sufficient to produce a block 80 long, 42.9 wide, and 34.8 high.
2. Machine the base block to the 80 length and 34.8 height, with the lower portion of the profile at 20 wide.
3. Add the upper shoulder so the profile steps from 20 wide to the full 42.9 width, with the step located 30 from the left end.
4. Extrude or form the stepped profile to the 34.8 height.
5. Drill the first hole at 10 from the left end and 10 from the front edge, using a 5 diameter.
6. Drill the second hole at 70 from the left end and 10 from the front edge, using a 5 diameter.
7. Apply a 2 radius fillet to the bottom vertical edges.

1. Start with stock sufficient to produce an 80 long by 42.9 high by 34.8 thick stepped plate.
2. Mill the lower step to the full 80 length and 34.8 thickness, with the step height set to 20.
3. Mill the upper step to the full 80 length and 34.8 thickness, with the step height set to 22.9, leaving the total height at 42.9.
4. Form the stepped profile so the lower step runs 25 from the left end and the upper step runs the remaining 55 to the right end.
5. Drill the first hole through the 34.8 thickness at the center of the lower step.
6. Drill the second hole through the 34.8 thickness at the center of the upper step.
7. Apply the R2.7 fillet to the vertical edge at the right end of the lower step.
8. Apply the R6.7 fillet to the vertical edge at the right end of the upper step.
9. Apply the R16.1 fillet to the vertical edge at the left end of the lower step.
10. Apply the R5.2 fillet to the vertical edge at the left end of the upper step.

1. Start with stock sized to the 80 overall length, 42.9 overall width, and 34.8 height.
2. Add material to form the main body as a solid block spanning the full 80 length and 34.8 height.
3. Shape the top profile so the left end rises to the 42.9 width, then steps down to a narrower shoulder.
4. Form the shoulder as a flat top section running most of the length, with a slight taper toward the right end.
5. Cut the right end to create the tapered nose, reducing the width from the shoulder down to the tip.
6. Apply the R16.1 fillet to the top-left corner where the full-width end meets the shoulder.
7. Apply the R6.7 fillet to the top-right corner where the shoulder meets the tapered nose.
8. Apply the R5.2 fillet to the bottom-right corner at the tip of the tapered nose.
9. Apply the R2.7 fillet to the bottom-left corner at the base of the full-width end.
10. Apply the 2× R5.4 fillets to the two bottom corners where the shoulder meets the base.

1. Start with stock sufficient to produce an 80 long by 42.9 wide by 34.8 high stepped block.
2. Mill the base profile to the 80 length and 42.9 overall width, leaving the stepped top contour unformed.
3. Add material to form the raised step along the top, establishing the 34.8 overall height.
4. Machine the step transition to the 20.8 dimension, defining the step location along the length.
5. Cut the step face to the 22.8 dimension, defining the step width.
6. Drill the first hole to the R16.1 radius at the step corner.
7. Drill the second hole to the R16.1 radius at the opposite step corner.
8. Drill the third hole to the R6.7 radius at the step end.
9. Drill the fourth hole to the R56.2 radius at the base corner.
10. Drill the fifth hole to the R2.7 radius at the remaining corner.
11. Apply the 2× R5.4 fillets to the two vertical edges at the step transition.

1. Saw the blank from plate stock to the printed 80 overall length and 34.8 thickness, leaving the profile slightly oversize.
2. Mill the base to a straight bottom edge running the full 80 length, with a straight top edge at the printed 20 height (half of the printed 42.9 overall height).
3. Mill the step so the raised section begins at the printed 25.7 from the left end, leaving the lower shoulder 25.7 long.
4. Mill the raised section's top edge to the printed 42.9 overall height, holding the printed 34.8 wall thickness.
5. Mill the right end face to the printed 42.9 overall height, leaving the raised section 54.3 long (80 minus 25.7).
6. Round the two vertical corners at the step with the printed 2× R5.4 fillets.
7. Round the two vertical corners at the right end with the printed R6.7 and R5.2 fillets.
8. Round the two vertical corners at the left end with the printed R16.1 and R2.7 fillets.

1. Start with stock sized to the 80 overall length, 42.9 overall height, and 34.8 depth.
2. Add material to form the main body as a solid block spanning the full 80 length and 34.8 depth, with the upper profile rising to the 42.9 height.
3. Shape the top edge so it runs flat from the left end to the step location, then rises to the full 42.9 height and continues to the right end.
4. Cut the step recess at the left end, leaving a lower shoulder 20 wide and 20 high, with the step positioned 20 in from the left end.
5. Drill the first hole at the location 20 from the left end and 20 from the bottom edge, using the 2× R5.4 callout for the two equal holes.
6. Drill the second hole at the location 20 from the right end and 20 from the bottom edge, matching the same 2× R5.4 size.
7. Apply the R16.1 fillet to the top edge where the step meets the full-height section.
8. Apply the R6.7 fillet to the top edge at the right end of the part.
9. Apply the R5.2 fillet to the bottom edge at the right end of the part.
10. Apply the R2.7 fillet to the bottom edge at the left end of the part.

1. Start with stock sufficient to form an X-shaped bracket with an overall envelope of 80 by 62.6.
2. Add material to form the first diagonal arm at 45 degrees, with a length of 80 and a width of 10.7.
3. Add material to form the second diagonal arm at -45 degrees, with a length of 80 and a width of 10.7.
4. Ensure the two arms intersect at the center to create the X shape.
5. Verify the overall height of the bracket is 62.6.
6. Apply a small chamfer to all edges to remove sharp corners.

1. Start with stock sufficient to produce an 80 long by 62.6 high by 10.7 thick bracket blank.
2. Machine the first diagonal leg as a rectangular bar 80 long, 62.6 high, and 10.7 thick, rotated 45 degrees about the thickness axis.
3. Machine the second diagonal leg identically at −45 degrees about the thickness axis.
4. Join the two legs at their common center to form the X-shaped bracket body.
5. Drill a through hole of diameter 5 at the center of the bracket, passing through the full 10.7 thickness.
6. Apply a 0.5 chamfer to all edges of the bracket.

1. Start with stock sufficient to form an X-shaped bracket with an overall envelope of 80 by 62.6.
2. Add material to form the first diagonal arm, 80 long, 10.7 wide, and 10.7 thick, oriented at 45 degrees.
3. Add material to form the second diagonal arm, 80 long, 10.7 wide, and 10.7 thick, oriented at -45 degrees, intersecting the first arm at its center.
4. Cut a through hole of diameter 5.5 at the center of the intersection.
5. Apply a chamfer of 0.5 to all edges of the bracket.

1. Start with stock sufficient to form an 80 long by 10.7 thick by 10.7 high rectangular arm.
2. Machine the first arm to the printed 80 length, 10.7 thickness, and 10.7 height.
3. Machine the second identical arm to the same printed 80 length, 10.7 thickness, and 10.7 height.
4. Position the second arm perpendicular to the first arm so their centerlines intersect at mid-length.
5. Join the two arms into a single rigid cross-shaped body.
6. Verify the overall envelope matches the printed 80 by 62.6 by 10.7 bounding dimensions.

1. Start with stock sufficient to produce an 80 long by 62.6 high by 10.7 thick plate.
2. Machine the plate to the 80 overall length and 62.6 overall height.
3. Mill the plate to the 10.7 thickness.
4. Cut the first diagonal arm across the plate at 45 degrees, using the 10.7 thickness as the arm width.
5. Cut the second diagonal arm across the plate at -45 degrees, using the 10.7 thickness as the arm width.
6. Remove the material outside the two diagonal arms to form the X-shaped profile.
7. Break all sharp edges with a small chamfer.

1. Start with stock sufficient to form an X-shaped bracket with an overall envelope of 80 by 62.6.
2. Add material to form the first diagonal leg, 80 long, 10.7 wide, and 10.7 thick, oriented at 45 degrees.
3. Add material to form the second diagonal leg, 80 long, 10.7 wide, and 10.7 thick, oriented at -45 degrees.
4. Fuse the two legs together at their intersection to create the X-shaped bracket.

1. Start with a rectangular block of stock measuring 10.7 units wide by 80 units long by 62.6 units tall.
2. Machine the block to the final overall dimensions of 10.7 by 80 by 62.6.
3. Cut a diagonal slot through the block at a 45-degree angle, with the slot width set to 10 units.
4. Cut a second diagonal slot through the block at a -45-degree angle, with the slot width set to 10 units.
5. Ensure both slots pass completely through the block, creating an X-shaped opening.
6. Verify the slots are centered and symmetrical about the block's centerline.
7. Deburr all edges and corners to remove any sharpness.

1. Start with stock sufficient to produce an 80 long by 10.7 thick by 62.6 tall X-shaped bracket blank.
2. Add material to form the first diagonal arm, 80 long, 10.7 thick, and 10.7 wide, oriented at 45 degrees.
3. Add material to form the second diagonal arm, 80 long, 10.7 thick, and 10.7 wide, oriented at -45 degrees.
4. Fuse the two diagonal arms at their centers to create the X-shaped bracket body.
5. Verify the overall height of the bracket is 62.6.
6. Verify the overall length of the bracket is 80.
7. Verify the bracket thickness is 10.7.

1. Start with a rectangular block of stock measuring 5.6 wide by 11.0 tall by 80 long.
2. Establish the 80 dimension as the overall length of the part.
3. Establish the 5.6 dimension as the overall width of the part.
4. Establish the 11.0 dimension as the overall height of the part.
5. Cut the block along a curved path to form the main body of the part.
6. The curved path has a radius of 40, derived from the 80 length and the 11.0 height.
7. The curved path is centered on the 5.6 width of the part.
8. The curved path is centered on the 11.0 height of the part.
9. The curved path is centered on the 80 length of the part.
10. The final part is a curved rectangular block with a 5.6 width, 11.0 height, and 80 length.

1. Start with a rectangular block of stock measuring 80.0 long by 12.0 wide by 5.6 thick.
2. Machine the block to the overall length of 80.0.
3. Machine the block to the overall width of 12.0.
4. Machine the block to the overall thickness of 5.6.
5. Form the curved profile by sweeping the rectangular section along a path with a radius of 40.0.
6. Set the sweep angle to 90.0 degrees to create the quarter-circle bend.
7. Apply a chamfer to the outer edges of the curved profile.
8. Set the chamfer distance to 1.0.
9. Apply a fillet to the inner edges of the curved profile.
10. Set the fillet radius to 0.5.

1. Start with stock sufficient to form a curved arm 80 long with a 121.7 A/F profile.
2. Form the main arm body as a curved sweep with a 5.6 thickness and 11.0 height.
3. Add a rectangular tab at the start of the arm, sized to the 5.6 thickness and 11.0 height.
4. Add a matching rectangular tab at the end of the arm, sized to the 5.6 thickness and 11.0 height.
5. Blend the tabs into the curved arm body so the overall length remains 80.
6. Verify the finished part against the 80 length, 121.7 A/F profile, 11.0 height, and 5.6 thickness.

1. Start with a rectangular bar of stock sized to the 80.0 overall length and the 11.0 maximum height.
2. Establish the part’s 5.6 thickness as the constant cross-section width.
3. Form the curved profile by sweeping a 5.6 by 11.0 rectangular section along a path that rises 80.0 overall.
4. Shape the path so the curve peaks at the 11.0 height at mid-length, then returns to a lower height at the far end.
5. Add material to build up the curved arm body from the swept profile.
6. Cut a rectangular pocket into the top face at the mid-length position.
7. Size the pocket to a width of 3.0 and a depth of 2.0.
8. Position the pocket so its center is located 40.0 from the start of the arm.
9. Chamfer the top edges of the arm with a 0.5 chamfer.
10. Deburr all remaining edges and verify the 80.0 length, 11.0 peak height, and 5.6 thickness.

1. Start with a rectangular block of stock measuring 5.6 wide by 11.0 tall by 80 long.
2. Machine the block to the overall length of 80.
3. Establish the cross-section of the part as 5.6 wide by 11.0 tall.
4. Form the curved profile of the part by sweeping the 5.6 by 11.0 cross-section along a path with a 121.7 A/F radius.
5. Ensure the curved profile maintains the 122.0 A/F dimension across the flats.
6. Verify the final part matches the dimensions shown on the drawing.

1. Start with a rectangular block of stock measuring 5.6 mm wide, 11.0 mm tall, and 80.0 mm long.

2. Establish the block as the base material with its full 80.0 mm length running along the primary axis.

3. Cut the block to a uniform thickness of 5.6 mm across its entire length.

4. Machine the top surface to a consistent height of 11.0 mm above the bottom face.

5. Shape the bottom profile as a smooth convex curve that spans the full 80.0 mm length, rising from the base to a maximum height of 11.0 mm at mid-length.

6. Form the top profile as a smooth concave curve that spans the full 80.0 mm length, dipping from the top surface to a minimum height of 5.6 mm at mid-length.

7. Ensure the two curved profiles meet at the ends of the 80.0 mm length, creating a closed cross-section.

8. Extrude the curved profile along the full 80.0 mm length to create the main body.

9. Apply a small chamfer to all edges running along the length of the part to break the sharp corners.

10. Verify the final dimensions: 80.0 mm overall length, 5.6 mm width, and 11.0 mm maximum height.

1. Start with a rectangular block of stock measuring 5.6 wide by 20.0 tall by 80.0 long.
2. Establish the 80.0 dimension as the overall length of the part.
3. Establish the 5.6 dimension as the overall width of the part.
4. Establish the 20.0 dimension as the overall height of the part.
5. Cut the block along a curved path to form the main body, with the curve spanning the full 80.0 length.
6. The curve has a radius of 121.7, creating a gentle arc through the part's height.
7. The curve's chord length is 11.0, defining the horizontal displacement between the start and end of the arc.
8. The curve's sagitta is 0.5, representing the maximum deviation from the chord line.
9. The curve's angle is 5.1 degrees, measured from the horizontal axis.
10. The final part is a curved rectangular bar with the specified dimensions.

1. Start with stock sufficient to form a curved rail 80 long, 11.0 wide, and 5.6 thick.
2. Form the rail body as a constant-section sweep of the 11.0 by 5.6 rectangular profile along a curved path.
3. Shape the path so the rail runs 80 in length with a 12.0 arc height, giving a 121.7 A/F overall span.
4. Add a small rounded transition at the top edge of the rail profile, with no printed size.
5. Cut a narrow longitudinal slot along the top of the rail, with no printed size.
6. Drill a small through hole near the top of the rail, with no printed size.
7. Apply a small chamfer to the top edges of the rail, with no printed size.

1. Start with stock sufficient to form a five-pointed star profile with an outer radius of 40.0 and an inner radius of 30.0.
2. Extrude the star profile to a height of 21.1 to create the main body.
3. Cut a hexagonal pocket with a radius of 15.0 to a depth of 15.0 from the top face.
4. Drill a through hole with a diameter of 22.4 through the center of the part.
5. Apply a fillet with a radius of 40.4 to the vertical edges of the star profile.

1. Start with a cylindrical blank of 80.0 mm diameter and 21.1 mm height.
2. Machine the outer profile to a five-pointed star shape with 40.0 mm outer radius and 30.0 mm inner radius, maintaining the 21.1 mm height.
3. Drill a central through-hole of ⌀22.4 mm diameter.
4. Cut a hexagonal socket into the top face with 15.0 mm across-flats dimension and 12.0 mm depth.
5. Apply a 1.0 mm chamfer to all vertical edges of the star profile.

1. Start with a five-pointed star plate stock, with the outer points at radius 40.0 and the inner valleys at radius 30.0.
2. Extrude the star profile to a height of 20.0.
3. Apply a 3× R40.4 fillet to the three outermost points of the star.
4. Drill a ⌀22.4 through hole at the center of the star.
5. Cut a hexagonal pocket from the top face, with a hexagon radius of 15.0 and a depth of 15.0.
6. Chamfer the top outer edges of the star by 1.0.

1. Start with a regular pentagonal plate blank whose five vertices lie on a 40.0 radius circle, giving the printed 80.0 across opposite corners and 73.1 across opposite flats, with a 40.4 distance from the center to each flat.
2. Extrude the pentagonal blank to the printed 21.1 plate thickness.
3. Drill the single ⌀22.4 through hole at the center of the plate.
4. Cut a regular hexagonal pocket from the top face, centered on the plate, with a 30.0 across-flats size and a depth of 15.0.
5. Apply the printed 3× R40.4 fillets to the three vertical edges of the pentagonal plate.

1. Start with a cylindrical blank of 80.0 mm diameter and 21.1 mm height.
2. Loft the outer profile from a circle of 40.0 mm radius at the base to a six-point star of 40.0 mm outer radius at the top, creating the main body.
3. Add a central boss of 20.0 mm radius and 10.0 mm height at the base.
4. Cut a hexagonal socket of 12.0 mm circumscribed radius and 15.0 mm depth into the top face.
5. Drill a through hole of 22.4 mm diameter through the entire part.
6. Apply a 2.0 mm chamfer to all vertical edges.

1. Start with stock sufficient to form a hexagonal prism 80.0 across the flats and 21.1 tall.
2. Machine the hexagonal outer profile to 80.0 across the flats, corresponding to a 40.0 circumradius.
3. Extrude the hexagonal profile to the 21.1 height.
4. Cut the central through hole to ⌀22.4, using a 11.2 radius.
5. Cut the hexagonal socket into the top face, sized qualitatively smaller than the outer hexagon and deep enough to leave the surrounding wall.
6. Apply the 3× R40.4 fillets to the three specified vertical edges.
7. Verify the 73.1 dimension across the relevant feature as shown on the drawing.
8. Verify the 40.4 dimension on the related feature as shown on the drawing.

1. Start with stock sufficient to contain an 80.0 mm diameter by 21.1 mm tall part.
2. Form the main body as a five-lobed star shape with 80.0 mm outer points and 73.1 mm inner valleys, extruded to a height of 21.1 mm.
3. Drill a through hole of ⌀22.4 mm (radius 11.2 mm) centered on the part axis.
4. Cut a hexagonal socket from the top face with a 30.0 mm across-corners size and a depth of 15.0 mm.
5. Apply a 1.0 mm chamfer to all vertical edges of the star body.

1. Start with a cylindrical blank of diameter 80.0 mm and height 21.1 mm.
2. Machine the outer profile into a five-pointed star shape with a 40.0 mm outer radius and a 30.0 mm inner radius.
3. Extrude the star profile to the full 21.1 mm height.
4. Drill a central through hole of diameter 22.4 mm.
5. Cut a hexagonal socket into the top face with a 20.0 mm circumscribed radius and a depth of 15.0 mm.
6. Chamfer all vertical edges with a 1.0 mm chamfer.

1. Start with cylindrical stock sized to the printed 80 outside diameter and 15.1 overall length.
2. Turn the outside diameter to the printed ø80.
3. Face the ends to establish the printed 15.1 length.
4. Bore the through hole to the printed ø37.7.
5. Machine the internal step to the printed ø64.9 diameter.
6. Set the step location from the printed 40 dimension.
7. Machine the step length from the printed 40 dimension.
8. Cut the internal relief to the printed 9.1 depth.
9. Apply the small edge fillet at the step transition.
10. Deburr all edges and verify the printed dimensions.

1. Start with cylindrical stock of 80 diameter and 15.1 thickness.
2. Turn the outer diameter to the printed ø80 callout.
3. Face the part to the printed 15.1 thickness.
4. Drill the central through hole to the printed ø37.7 diameter.
5. Machine the internal annular groove to the printed ø64.9 diameter, leaving a 9.1 wide land from the outer edge.
6. Cut the groove to a depth of 40 from the top face.
7. Apply a 7.5 radius fillet to the outer top edge.
8. Apply a 7.5 radius fillet to the inner top edge.
9. Apply a 7.5 radius fillet to the groove top edge.
10. Deburr all remaining sharp edges.

1. Start with cylindrical stock sized to the printed ø80 outside diameter and 15.1 overall length.
2. Turn the outside diameter to the printed ø80.
3. Face the part to the printed 15.1 length.
4. Bore the through hole to the printed 1× ⌀64.9 callout.
5. Cut the internal groove to the printed ø37.7 diameter.
6. Machine the groove to the printed 9.1 width.
7. Position the groove at the printed 40 location from the reference face.
8. Machine the second printed 40 dimension to establish the remaining axial reference.
9. Apply the printed R7.5 fillet to the outer edge.
10. Deburr all edges and verify the printed dimensions.

1. Saw a blank from round bar stock with enough diameter to clean up at the printed ø80 and enough length to face back to the printed 15.1 overall width.
2. Chuck the blank, face one end, and turn the outside down to the printed ø80, working to the printed 40 outer radius.
3. Face the second end to bring the ring to the printed 15.1 width.
4. Drill and bore the central through hole to the printed ø37.7.
5. From the front face, counterbore the single printed 1× ⌀64.9 hole to the printed 9.1 depth, leaving the back face open.
6. Mill the small rectangular pocket into the front face at the printed 40 location, sized and positioned per the drawing.
7. Break the sharp edges on the front face with a small chamfer.
8. Deburr the bore, counterbore, and pocket, then clean the part.

1. Start with a solid cylindrical blank of 80 mm diameter and 15.1 mm thickness.
2. Turn the outer diameter to the printed ø80 callout.
3. Face the blank to the printed 15.1 mm thickness.
4. Drill and bore the central through hole to the printed ø37.7 callout.
5. Machine the internal groove to the printed 1× ⌀64.9 callout, cutting to a depth of 9.1 mm.
6. Apply a small chamfer to the outer rim edges to break the sharp corners.

1. Start with a solid cylindrical blank of 80 mm diameter and 15.1 mm thickness.
2. Turn the outer diameter to the printed ø80 callout.

1. Start with a rectangular block of stock measuring 19.2 wide by 5.8 thick by 79.9 tall.

1. Start with a rectangular block of stock measuring 19.2 wide by 5.8 thick by 79.9 tall.

1. Saw a rectangular blank from plate stock with enough envelope to contain the finished arm's 79.9 overall length, 19.2 overall width, and 5.8 thickness.

6. Drill two through holes of 3.0 mm diameter, spaced 20.0 mm apart along the centerline.
7. Apply a 0.5 mm chamfer to all outer edges.
8. Apply a 0.3 mm fillet to the slot edges.

1. Start with stock sufficient to form a three-lobed plate with an overall envelope of 80.0 by 73.2.
2. Form the first lobe as a cylinder of diameter 29.6 (radius 14.8) centered at the origin.
3. Form the second lobe as a cylinder of diameter 29.6 centered at a distance of 29.3 from the origin along the vertical axis.
4. Form the third lobe as a cylinder of diameter 29.6 centered at a distance of 29.3 from the origin along the horizontal axis.
5. Extrude the combined lobes to a thickness of 6.6.
6. Drill the central through hole of diameter 21.1.
7. Drill the first of the three equally spaced through holes of diameter 21.1 on a bolt circle of diameter 58.2 (radius 29.1).
8. Drill the second of the three equally spaced through holes of diameter 21.1 on the same bolt circle.
9. Drill the third of the three equally spaced through holes of diameter 21.1 on the same bolt circle.
10. Apply a fillet of radius 1.9 to all edges of the plate.

1. Start with stock sufficient to form a tri-lobed plate with an overall envelope of 80.0 by 73.2 and a thickness of 6.6.
2. Form the outer profile as three lobes of radius 14.8 (derived from the printed ø29.6) arranged at 120-degree intervals, with the lobes centered on a 29.1 radius (derived from the printed 58.2 bolt circle) from the part center.
3. Extrude the profile to the printed thickness of 6.6.
4. Drill the central through hole to the printed ⌀21.1.
5. Drill the three outer through holes to the printed ⌀21.1, positioned at the printed 29.3 offset from the part center (derived from the printed 58.2 bolt circle and the lobe geometry).
6. Apply the printed 6× R1.9 fillets to the six outer edges of the lobes.

1. Start with stock sufficient to form a three-lobed plate with an overall envelope of 80.0 by 73.2 and a thickness of 6.6.
2. Form the first lobe as a circle of diameter 29.6 centered at the origin.
3. Form the second lobe as a circle of diameter 29.6 centered at a distance of 29.3 from the origin along the vertical axis.
4. Form the third lobe as a circle of diameter 29.6 centered at a distance of 29.3 from the origin along the horizontal axis.
5. Form the fourth lobe as a circle of diameter 29.6 centered at a distance of 29.3 from the origin along the opposite horizontal axis.
6. Extrude the combined lobes to the plate thickness of 6.6.
7. Drill the central through hole with a diameter of 21.1.
8. Drill the first of the three equally spaced through holes with a diameter of 21.1 at a radius of 29.1 from the center.
9. Drill the second of the three equally spaced through holes with a diameter of 21.1 at a radius of 29.1 from the center.
10. Drill the third of the three equally spaced through holes with a diameter of 21.1 at a radius of 29.1 from the center.
11. Apply a fillet of radius 1.9 to all outer edges of the plate.

1. Start with a flat plate of stock material with a thickness of 6.6.
2. Machine the outer profile to form a three-lobed circular shape, with each lobe having a diameter of 29.6.
3. Position the lobes at a distance of 29.3 from the center of the part.
4. Drill a central through hole with a diameter of 21.1.
5. Drill three through holes, each with a diameter of 21.1, located at a distance of 29.3 from the center.
6. Apply a fillet with a radius of 1.9 to all outer edges of the lobes.

1. Start with stock sufficient to form a three-lobed plate measuring 80.0 across the widest lobes and 73.2 across the other axis, with a thickness of 6.6.
2. Add material to form the outer profile as three overlapping lobes, each with a diameter of 29.6, arranged at 120-degree intervals around the center.
3. Position the lobes so their centers are spaced 29.3 from the part center, creating the overall 80.0 and 73.2 envelope dimensions.
4. Drill the central through hole with a diameter of 21.1.
5. Drill three additional through holes with a diameter of 21.1, one in each lobe, positioned at the same 29.3 offset from the center.
6. Apply a fillet with a radius of 1.9 to all edges, as indicated by the 6× R1.9 callout.

1. Start with flat plate stock at the printed 6.6 thickness.
2. Lay out the three-hole pattern as an equilateral triangle with 58.2 center-to-center spacing, derived as twice the printed 29.3.
3. Add material to form three lobes of ø29.6 (radius 14.8) centered on the triangle vertices.
4. Add material to form the central hub of ø21.1 (radius 10.55) at the triangle center.
5. Drill the central through hole of ø21.1 per the 1× ⌀21.1 THRU callout.
6. Drill the three outer through holes of ø21.1 per the 3× ⌀21.1 THRU callout, centered on the lobe centers.
7. Fillet all edges to the printed 6× R1.9 radius.

1. Start with flat stock at least 80.0 wide by 73.2 high and 6.6 thick.
2. Add material to form a central circular hub of diameter 29.6 (radius 14.8) at the part center.
3. Add three arms of diameter 29.6 (radius 14.8) extending from the hub at 120° intervals, each centered 29.3 from the part center.
4. Drill the central through hole of diameter 21.1.
5. Drill three through holes of diameter 21.1, one in each arm, centered 29.3 from the part center.
6. Apply a 1.9 radius fillet to all six outer edges of the arms.

1. Start with flat plate stock 6.6 thick, sawn to a blank slightly larger than the 80.0 overall envelope.
2. Mill the blank to the three-lobed outline, holding the 80.0 overall width across the two lower lobes and the 73.2 overall height to the top of the upper lobe.
3. Form each of the three lobes as a ø29.6 round, with the two lower lobes centered 40.0 apart on the horizontal centerline and the upper lobe centered on the vertical centerline.
4. Position the upper lobe so its center sits 29.3 above the horizontal centerline, leaving the lower lobes 29.3 below it.
5. Drill and bore the central through hole to ⌀21.1.
6. Drill and bore the three matching ⌀21.1 through holes, one centered in each lobe.
7. Apply the 6× R1.9 fillets to the six re-entrant corners where the lobes meet.
8. Deburr all hole edges and verify the 6.6 thickness is uniform across the part.

1. Start with a cylindrical blank of 80.0 mm diameter and 9.6 mm thickness.
2. Add eight equally spaced cylindrical lobes of 22.7 mm diameter around the outer edge of the blank, each with the same 9.6 mm thickness.
3. Drill a central through hole of 26.7 mm diameter.
4. Drill eight equally spaced through holes of 12.4 mm diameter on a 57.3 mm diameter bolt circle.
5. Drill sixteen equally spaced through holes of 11.7 mm diameter on a 57.3 mm diameter bolt circle.

1. Start with cylindrical stock sized to the 80.0 mm overall envelope and faced to the 9.0 mm thickness.
2. Turn the outer profile to the 80.0 mm diameter, establishing the 40.0 mm outer radius.
3. Bore the central through hole to the 26.7 mm diameter, leaving the annular ring body.
4. Machine the 16 equally spaced radial slots, each 11.0 mm wide, centered on the 28.65 mm pitch circle radius derived from the 11.3 mm and 60.3 mm callouts.

6. Drill the 8 equally spaced through holes at 12.4 mm diameter on the 28.65 mm pitch circle radius.
7. Drill the 16 equally spaced through holes at 11.7 mm diameter on the same 28.65 mm pitch circle radius.
8. Break all sharp edges with a small chamfer on the outer rim, inner bore, and slot edges.

1. Start with a cylindrical stock of diameter 80.0 and thickness 9.6.
2. Add eight lobes of diameter 22.7, each with a radius of 11.35, positioned at a distance of 28.65 from the center.
3. Drill a central hole of diameter 26.7 through the part.
4. Drill sixteen holes of diameter 11.7 through the part, arranged in a circular pattern.
5. Drill eight holes of diameter 12.4 through the part, arranged in a circular pattern.

1. Start with stock sufficient to form a circular plate of diameter 80.0 (derived from the printed 40.0 radius) and thickness 9.6.
2. Turn or mill the outer profile to the 80.0 diameter and face the plate to the 9.6 thickness.
3. Drill and bore the central through hole to the printed 1× ⌀26.7 callout.
4. Lay out the eight equally spaced hole positions on a bolt circle of diameter 57.3 (derived from the printed 28.65 radius).
5. Drill the eight through holes to the printed 8× ⌀12.4 callout.
6. Lay out the sixteen equally spaced hole positions on a bolt circle of diameter 57.3 (derived from the printed 28.65 radius).
7. Drill the sixteen through holes to the printed 16× ⌀11.7 callout.
8. Verify the hole pattern spacing using the printed 11.3, 40.0, and 60.3 dimensions to confirm the radial and axial locations of the hole groups.
9. Deburr all hole edges and the outer profile.
10. Inspect the part against the drawing to confirm all dimensions meet the specified callouts.

1. Start with a cylindrical blank of 80 mm diameter and 9.6 mm thickness.
2. Drill a central through hole of 26.7 mm diameter.
3. Drill 8 through holes of 12.4 mm diameter on a 57.3 mm diameter bolt circle.
4. Drill 16 through holes of 11.7 mm diameter on a 57.3 mm diameter bolt circle, alternating with the 12.4 mm holes.
5. Chamfer all outer edges of the blank.

1. Start with stock sufficient to form a ring of 8 equally spaced circular lobes, each with a diameter of 22.7, arranged on a 40.0 center-to-center spacing.
2. Add material to form the 8 lobes as solid cylinders of diameter 22.7 and height 9.6, positioned at a radius of 20.0 from the center.
3. Add a central cylindrical hub of diameter 22.7 and height 9.6 at the center of the ring.
4. Drill 8 through holes of diameter 12.4, each centered on a lobe at a radius of 20.0 from the center.
5. Drill 16 through holes of diameter 11.7, each centered on a lobe at a radius of 20.0 from the center.
6. Drill 1 through hole of diameter 26.7 at the center of the hub.
7. Apply a small chamfer to all vertical edges of the lobes and hub.

1. Start with stock sufficient to form a 9.6-thick disc with an 80.0 overall diameter.
2. Turn or mill the outer profile to the 80.0 diameter and face the disc to the 9.6 thickness.
3. Drill and bore the central through hole to ⌀26.7.
4. Lay out the 16-hole pattern on a ⌀57.3 bolt circle, equally spaced at 22.5° intervals.
5. Drill the 16 through holes to ⌀11.7.
6. Lay out the 8-hole pattern on the same ⌀57.3 bolt circle, equally spaced at 45° intervals and offset 22.5° from the 16-hole pattern.
7. Drill the 8 through holes to ⌀12.4.
8. Deburr all holes and break sharp edges.

1. Start with a cylindrical blank of diameter 80.0 and thickness 9.6.
2. Cut a central through hole of diameter 26.7.
3. Add eight lobes of diameter 22.7, each centered on a circle of radius 28.65 (derived from the printed 57.3 bolt circle diameter), spaced at 45-degree intervals around the center.
4. Cut eight through holes of diameter 12.4, each centered on the same circle of radius 28.65, spaced at 45-degree intervals.
5. Cut sixteen through holes of diameter 11.7, each centered on a circle of radius 19.1 (derived from the printed 38.2 bolt circle diameter), spaced at 22.5-degree intervals around the center.

1. Start with cylindrical stock sized to the largest printed diameter, ø20.6, and long enough to cover the full 100 mm arm length.
2. Turn the main arm body to the printed ø20.6 diameter over the full 100 mm length.
3. Turn the tapered nose from the printed ø20.6 down to the printed ø6.0 over the printed 30 mm nose length.
4. Turn the reduced end section to the printed ø14.7 diameter for the printed 20 mm length at the far end of the arm.
5. Add the circumferential rib at the printed 60 mm position from the nose end, with the printed 5 mm width and the printed 2 mm height.
6. Drill the first set of three radial holes at the printed 40 mm position from the nose end, using the printed ø4.0 diameter and the printed 8 mm depth.
7. Drill the second set of three radial holes at the printed 70 mm position from the nose end, using the printed ø4.0 diameter and the printed 8 mm depth.
8. Apply the printed 1 mm chamfer to the outer edge of the reduced end section.

1. Start with cylindrical stock sized to the largest printed diameter, ø20.6, and cut it to the overall length of 80.
2. Turn the main body to the printed ø20.6 diameter for the full 80 length.

1. Saw a blank from round bar stock with enough diameter to clean up at the printed ø20.6 and enough length to face back to the finished 52.0 overall.
2. Face both ends of the blank to the 52.0 overall length.
3. Turn the main body to the printed ø20.6, i.e. a 10.3 radius.

7. Drill the small through hole along the axis of the part.
8. Mill the evenly spaced slots around the body at the printed 2.1 × 2.4 × 3 DEEP size, cutting each slot 3 deep.

1. Start with round stock sized to the largest printed diameter, ø20.6, and face it to the overall length of 80.0.
2. Turn the main body to the printed ø20.6 diameter for the full 80.0 length.

8. Drill the third cross hole through the body at the printed 60.0 location from the front end, using the printed ø4.0 diameter.

1. Start with cylindrical stock sized to the largest printed diameter, ø18.1, and long enough to cover the full 100 mm rod length.

1. Start with stock sufficient to form a revolved shaft of overall length 68.2 mm, derived from the printed 16.2 mm and 52.0 mm axial dimensions.

1. Start with round stock sized to the largest printed diameter, ø18.1, and cut it to the overall length of 80.0, derived as the sum of the printed 16.2, 52.0, and 11.8.

1. Saw a blank from round bar stock with enough diameter to clean up at the largest printed size, the ø20.6 head, and enough length to face both ends.
2. Face the blank square and establish the datum end, then turn the head to ø20.6 for a length of 20.6 from that end.

5. Mill the keyway slot into the shank, 6.5 wide by 3.4 deep, centered 32.5 from the head shoulder.
6. Drill the set-screw hole radially into the head at mid-length, 10.3 in from the head shoulder, and countersink the mouth to seat the screw head.
7. Break all sharp edges and deburr the keyway and the set-screw hole.

1. Start with a rectangular plate blank 80.0 long by 27.8 wide by 3.0 thick.

1. Start with a rectangular plate blank 80.0 long by 27.8 wide by 4.0 thick.

1. Start with a rectangular plate blank 80.0 long by 27.8 wide by 2.0 thick.

1. Start with a rectangular plate blank 80.0 long by 27.8 wide by 3.0 thick.

1. Start with stock sufficient to form a 58.1 mm tall part with a 40 mm radius base.
2. Add material to form the base cylinder with a 40 mm radius and 26.4 mm height.

1. Start with stock sufficient to form a 12-sided polygonal base with a 40 mm circumradius, giving the printed 80.0 mm across-corner dimension.
2. Extrude the 12-sided base profile to a height of 26.0 mm, derived as the printed 58.1 mm total height minus the printed 31.7 mm top-feature height.

1. Start with cylindrical stock of 80 mm diameter and 20 mm height.

1. Saw a blank from round bar stock, leaving enough diameter to clean up at the printed 58.1 tooth-tip diameter and enough length to face both ends.
2. Chuck the blank and face the ends square to the printed 58.1 overall height.
3. Turn the lower register down to the printed 31.7 radius, stopping at the printed 31.7 height so the register runs from the base up to that shoulder.
4. Leave the upper portion at the printed 25.1 radius — the printed 58.1 less the printed 31.7 — forming the hexagonal boss that rises from the register to the top face.
5. Mill the six equally spaced flats around the boss to the printed 50.3 across-flats size, taking each flat down to the printed 25.15 from center.
6. Cut the twelve evenly spaced teeth around the register, each tooth running the full register height and reaching the printed 58.1 tip diameter.
7. Chamfer the twelve tooth roots at the printed C2.6, one chamfer callout per tooth.
8. Break the sharp edges at the top rim and the register shoulder with a light chamfer.

1. Start with stock sufficient to contain the 80 mm diameter gear blank and the 58.1 mm overall height.

5. Drill the central through hole to the 10 mm diameter.
6. Apply the C2.6 chamfer to the bottom outer edge of the gear.

1. Start with a cylindrical stock blank of 80.0 diameter and 25.0 height.
2. Add twelve equally spaced ribs around the outer circumference, each rib 5.0 wide, 8.0 tall, and extending the full 25.0 height of the base.
3. Position the ribs so their outer faces reach a 40.0 radius from the center, matching the printed 80.0 overall diameter.
4. On top of the base, add a hexagonal boss with a 30.0 radius and a height of 30.0.
5. Ensure the hexagon's flat-to-flat dimension measures 50.3 as printed.
6. Apply a 2.6 chamfer to all edges of the bottom face, as indicated by the three C2.6 callouts.
7. Verify the overall height of the part is 58.1, which is the sum of the 25.0 base height and the 30.0 boss height, plus the 3.1 difference from the printed value.

1. Start with a cylindrical stock blank of 80.0 diameter and 58.1 height.
2. Form the lower body as a 12-sided polygon with 80.0 across flats, extruded to a height of 26.4.
3. Form the upper body as a 6-sided polygon with 50.3 across flats, extruded to a height of 31.7 and positioned on top of the lower body.
4. Chamfer the bottom edges of the lower body with a C2.6 chamfer.
